frameworks.name: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
frameworks.outcome: The substantial reduction of disaster risk and losses in lives, livelihoods and health and in the economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets of persons, businesses, communities and countries.
frameworks.goal: Prevent new and reduce existing disaster risk through the implementation of integrated and inclusive economic, structural, legal, social, health, cultural, educational, environmental, technological, political and institutional measures that prevent and reduce hazard exposure and vulnerability to disaster, increase preparedness for response and recovery, and thus strengthen resilience.

frameworks.name: Framework for Resilient Development in the Pacific
frameworks.vision: Pacific people, societies, economies, cultures and natural environments are resilient to changing conditions and extreme events from climate change, climate variability and geological processes, enhancing well-being and promoting sustainable development.
frameworks.purpose: The FRDP guides all stakeholders' actions to strengthen resilience by providing coordinated priorities for implementation at regional, national and community levels; a regional approach to address national priorities; awareness of vulnerability and resilience issues; a framework for support (finance, technology, capacity-building); partnership and collaboration mechanisms; and a framework for monitoring progress. It also contributes to implementing commitments under the SDGs, Sendai Framework, SAMOA Pathway, UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement.

frameworks.name: National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy
frameworks.objective: Enable Fiji to deliver its priority of preventing new disaster risk and reducing existing disaster risk in line with relevant regional and global frameworks (the Sendai Framework for DRR 2015-2030, the Sustainable Development Agenda 2015-2030, and the Framework for Resilient Development in the Pacific).
frameworks.goal: Stronger disaster risk governance and disaster risk reduction measures as part of the overall national effort towards sustainable and resilient development, supporting poverty alleviation.

frameworks.name: Fiji National Development Plan
frameworks.vision: The NDP 2025-2029 is founded on the vision of empowering the people of Fiji through unity, translated through 3 pillars: economic resilience, people empowerment and good governance, with the ultimate goal of improving social wellbeing and bringing greater prosperity to the people and the nation.
frameworks.vision2050: Fiji aspires to be a prosperous, inclusive and sustainable nation by 2050 — a high-income, advanced economy, a regional leader in innovation and technology, with modern infrastructure, environmental stewardship, high moral and ethical values, rich culture and heritage, excellence in sports, extensive international diplomacy, and entrenched high standards of governance. It will be realised through successive medium-term national development plans.
frameworks.mission: The Government prioritises the needs of all the people of Fiji at the centre of its national development policy and planning.

goals.title: Strengthened Integrated Adaptation and Risk Reduction to Enhance Resilience to Climate Change and Disasters
goals.contextSummary: Pacific Island countries and territories (PICTs) are among the most vulnerable in the world to climate change and disasters. While exposure levels are similar, vulnerability differs due to specific environmental, social and economic challenges that limit capacity. Since 1950, extreme events have affected approximately 9.2 million people in the Pacific with 9,811 deaths and USD 3.2 billion in damages; some PICTs have experienced natural disaster losses approaching or exceeding GDP. Low-intensity events generate cumulative losses equivalent to or exceeding those of single large disasters. Resilient development must extend beyond worsening extreme events and climate change impacts to address the underlying causes of vulnerability. PICTs need support to engage with the Warsaw International Mechanism for Loss and Damage.
goals.strategicObjective: Present and future disaster risk and climate change are successfully managed, in an integrated manner where possible, within social and economic development planning processes and practices, to build resilience.
goals.outcome: Stronger and more resilient communities where efficiencies are achieved by pursuing a more integrated approach to climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction.

goals.title: Low Carbon Development
goals.contextSummary: The Pacific Islands region contributes only 0.03 per cent of the world's total greenhouse gas emissions yet is among the most vulnerable to its effects. Important synergies exist between low carbon development and resilience building. PICTs are minimising emissions through commitments reflected in the Majuro Declaration, the Framework for Action on Energy Security in the Pacific, and NDCs. Oil is the main energy source meeting over two-thirds of energy demand, and petroleum price increases have cost most PICTs about 10% of gross national incomes. Total energy supply grew at 4.6% per year from 1990-2010 with carbon dioxide emissions growing by 3.9%. The greatest opportunities for reducing emissions are in electricity generation, transport and industrial sectors, with energy efficiency being most cost-effective.
goals.strategicObjective: More efficient end-use energy consumption, reduced carbon intensity of development processes, increased conservation of terrestrial and marine ecosystems and increased resilience of energy infrastructure in PICTs.
goals.outcome: Improved energy security, decreased net emissions of greenhouse gases, and enhanced resilience of energy infrastructure.

goals.title: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
goals.contextSummary: Coordinated and collaborative humanitarian action is vital to avoid duplication and enhance collective efforts to support PICTs in disaster preparedness, response and recovery. An enabling environment with political will is needed to build capacity of all relevant government agencies, development partners and humanitarian actors to respond to slow and sudden onset hazards in a coordinated and integrated manner. Support is needed for line ministries to lead sector-level actions, for national disaster management offices to coordinate overall response, and for interoperability of key response agencies. Local-level first responders and partners must adopt more coordinated approaches. A common framework for preparedness will enhance response capacities by maximising use of resources and expertise through the UNOCHA-led Pacific Humanitarian Team and other partners. Knowledge brokering, communication and access to meteorological, climate and geological information are essential across the humanitarian-development continuum.
goals.strategicObjective: Improved capacity of PICTs to prepare for emergencies and disasters, thereby ensuring timely and effective response and recovery, and to ensure future risk is reduced, in relation to both rapid and slow onset disasters.
goals.outcome: Disaster preparedness, response and recovery initiatives prevent undue human losses and suffering, and minimise adverse consequences for national, provincial, local and community economic, social and environmental systems.

priorities.title: Understanding disaster risk
priorities.summary: Policies and practices for disaster risk management should be based on an understanding of disaster risk in all its dimensions of vulnerability, capacity, exposure of persons and assets, hazard characteristics and the environment, to be used for pre-disaster risk assessment, prevention, mitigation and effective response.

priorities.title: Strengthening disaster risk governance to manage disaster risk
priorities.summary: Disaster risk governance at national, regional and global levels is of great importance for effective and efficient management of disaster risk, requiring clear vision, plans, competence, guidance and coordination within and across sectors and participation of relevant stakeholders to foster collaboration across mechanisms and institutions.

priorities.title: Investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience
priorities.summary: Public and private investment in disaster risk prevention and reduction through structural and non-structural measures are essential to enhance the economic, social, health and cultural resilience of persons, communities, countries and their assets as well as the environment, serving as drivers of innovation, growth and job creation while being cost-effective and instrumental to save lives.

priorities.title: Enhancing disaster preparedness for effective response and to 'Build Back Better' in recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction
priorities.summary: The steady growth of disaster risk indicates the need to further strengthen disaster preparedness for response, take action in anticipation of events, and ensure capacities are in place for effective response and recovery, with women and persons with disabilities empowered to lead and promote equitable and accessible approaches, and recovery phases leveraged to 'Build Back Better' by integrating disaster risk reduction into development.

strategies.title: Mainstreaming Disaster Risk Reduction
strategies.summary: Integrate DRR considerations into sustainable development policies, planning, programmes and financing at all levels of government. Key actions include reviewing the NDMA, setting up clear demarcation of DRR responsibilities among national and local governments, developing national and local action plans and SOPs, joint mainstreaming of DRR and CCA, and structural reforms to consolidate DRR organisations including establishing a focal point agency under the Office of the Prime Minister.

strategies.title: Disaster Risk Governance
strategies.summary: Establish a system of institutions, mechanisms, policies and legal frameworks to guide, coordinate and oversee DRR. Applies principles of good governance (transparency, effectiveness, strategic focus, sustainability, equity, rule of law, and political/legal feasibility). Strengthen disaster risk governance at preparedness, response, recovery and reconstruction stages, with national government as primary duty bearer and local governments playing key roles in land use planning, infrastructure maintenance, and enforcement of building codes.

strategies.title: Financing and Investing
strategies.summary: Secure sufficient proactive investment in DRR measures within annual government budgets, recognizing that pre-investment cost is lower than post-disaster response cost. Priorities structural measures for Disaster Risk-I category in urban areas first, then Disaster Risk-II in urban areas, then rural areas. Calls for establishment of recovery and reconstruction subsidy, disaster relief, collective relocation subsidy, funding loan, and disaster moratorium programmes, along with introduction of disaster insurance and social agreement on cost-sharing for disaster risks.

strategies.title: Preparedness
strategies.summary: Activate strong processes for preparedness through structural measures (flood control embankments, retention dams, drainage networks, mangrove planting, sea walls, safer schools and hospitals, evacuation centres) and non-structural measures (DRR education, improving regulatory environment, disaster risk assessment, building code updates, hazard monitoring and warning systems, business continuity plans, and continuous public awareness-raising through 'no regrets' strategies).

strategies.title: Emergency Response
strategies.summary: Execute well-coordinated humanitarian emergency response through the Disaster Risk Information System (DRIS) comprising information collection, analysis, dissemination and management sub-systems. Streamline early warning systems for evacuation, establish institutional reporting arrangements, clarify SOPs with rescue-and-relief principles and timelines, and strengthen the Fiji Cluster System for humanitarian response coordination with inclusion of all stakeholders and the Protection Code of Conduct for Humanitarian Workers.

strategies.title: Recovery and Reconstruction
strategies.summary: Provide livelihood support to disaster victims and resume productive activities during recovery stage, with streamlined Fiji Cluster System and improved shelter conditions. At reconstruction stage, formulate national reconstruction plans based on PDNA and DLDA outcomes, with Build Back Better (BBB) as the goal for infrastructure, houses and production facilities. Use public emergency broadcasting system for information dissemination and generate broad national understanding of reconstruction objectives.

strategies.title: Knowledge and Information
strategies.summary: Improve knowledge, information, attitudes and practices on how to respond to and reduce disaster risk. Leverage traditional wisdom and customs (e.g., traditional Fijian bures with cyclone-resistant design), implement DRR education to cultivate disaster information literacy, cultivate culture of community volunteering, wage tree-planting campaigns, convene regular CCA/DRR roundtable meetings, improve broadcast programmes, draw up an overall picture of DRR measures, and develop a 'Disaster Risk Reduction White Paper for Fiji'.

principles.label: (a)
principles.summary: Each State has the primary responsibility to prevent and reduce disaster risk, including through international, regional, subregional, transboundary and bilateral cooperation, with developing countries' efforts enhanced through sustainable international cooperation.

principles.label: (b)
principles.summary: Responsibilities for disaster risk reduction should be shared by central Governments and relevant national authorities, sectors and stakeholders, as appropriate to their national circumstances and governance systems.

principles.label: (c)
principles.summary: Managing disaster risk is aimed at protecting persons and their property, health, livelihoods and productive assets, as well as cultural and environmental assets, while promoting and protecting all human rights, including the right to development.

principles.label: (d)
principles.summary: Disaster risk reduction requires an all-of-society engagement and partnership, inclusive and non-discriminatory participation, with special attention to disproportionately affected people, and integration of gender, age, disability and cultural perspectives in all policies and practices.

principles.label: (e)
principles.summary: Disaster risk reduction and management depends on coordination mechanisms within and across sectors and with relevant stakeholders at all levels, requiring full engagement of all State institutions and clear articulation of responsibilities across public and private stakeholders.

principles.label: (f)
principles.summary: While national and federal State Governments retain the enabling, guiding and coordinating role, it is necessary to empower local authorities and communities to reduce disaster risk through resources, incentives and decision-making responsibilities.

principles.label: (g)
principles.summary: Disaster risk reduction requires a multi-hazard approach and inclusive risk-informed decision-making based on open exchange of disaggregated data and accessible, up-to-date, comprehensible, science-based risk information, complemented by traditional knowledge.

principles.label: (h)
principles.summary: Policies, plans, practices and mechanisms should aim at coherence across sustainable development, food security, health and safety, climate change, environmental management and disaster risk reduction agendas, as disaster risk reduction is essential to achieve sustainable development.

principles.label: (i)
principles.summary: While the drivers of disaster risk may be local, national, regional or global in scope, disaster risks have local and specific characteristics that must be understood for determining measures to reduce disaster risk.

principles.label: (j)
principles.summary: Addressing underlying disaster risk factors through risk-informed public and private investments is more cost-effective than primary reliance on post-disaster response and recovery, and contributes to sustainable development.

principles.label: (k)
principles.summary: In the post-disaster recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction phase, it is critical to prevent the creation of new risk and reduce existing risk by 'Building Back Better' and increasing public education and awareness of disaster risk.

principles.label: (l)
principles.summary: An effective and meaningful global partnership and the further strengthening of international cooperation, including fulfilment of official development assistance commitments by developed countries, are essential for effective disaster risk management.

principles.label: (m)
principles.summary: Developing countries, particularly the least developed, small island developing States, landlocked developing countries and African countries, need adequate, sustainable and timely support from developed countries and partners tailored to their needs and priorities.

principles.label: Integrate climate change and disaster risk management and mainstream into develo
principles.summary: Climate change and disaster risk management should be integrated where possible and mainstreamed into development planning, policy making, financing, programming and implementation to build resilience.

principles.label: Strengthen and develop partnerships across countries and territories
principles.summary: Partnerships and sharing of lessons learned and best practices should be strengthened across countries and territories, without compromising sovereignty and related considerations.

principles.label: Protect human rights
principles.summary: Human rights such as the right to life, safety, dignity, non-discrimination and access to basic necessities must be protected, ensuring every person has equitable access to humanitarian and development assistance according to their specific needs.

principles.label: Prioritise the needs and respect the rights of the most vulnerable and integrate
principles.summary: The needs of the most vulnerable (including women, persons with disabilities, children, youth and older persons) must be prioritised, their rights respected, and their effective participation facilitated. Gender considerations should be integrated with equitable participation of men and women in planning and implementation.

principles.label: Ensure resilient development is sustainable and aims to alleviate poverty and ha
principles.summary: Resilient development must be sustainable and contribute to alleviating poverty and hardship.

principles.label: Incorporate ecosystem-based services and functions in resilience building
principles.summary: Ecosystem-based services and functions should be incorporated into all resilience-building efforts.

principles.label: Advocate open and ready access to reliable sources of traditional and contempora
principles.summary: Open and ready access to reliable traditional and contemporary information sources should be advocated.

principles.label: Build on and reinforce cultural and traditional resilience and knowledge of comm
principles.summary: Cultural and traditional resilience and knowledge of communities should be built upon and reinforced, engaging communities as key actors in designing plans, activities and solutions relevant to them.

principles.label: Acknowledge and factor traditional worldview where spirituality plays an integra
principles.summary: Traditional worldview where spirituality plays an integral role in constructing a meaningful life and pro-active existence should be acknowledged and factored into resilience-building.

principles.title: Capacity Development
principles.summary: Enhance the DRR abilities of national and local government officials, civil society organisations, private sector, mass media, academia and the public through knowledge of hazards, vulnerability, exposure, coping capacity, risk governance, and DRR measures. Emphasizes trainers' training, South-South cooperation, and building capacity of local governments as the tier closest to communities.

principles.title: Participatory Approaches
principles.summary: Require all-of-society engagement and partnership (whole-of-society approach) through empowerment and inclusive, accessible, non-discriminatory participation, paying special attention to people disproportionately affected by disasters. Promotes DRR education, community-led mechanisms, new livelihood means, and inclusion of women, children, and persons with disabilities.

principles.title: Human Rights and Gender Based Approaches
principles.summary: Promote broad popular participation and active roles of vulnerable groups through human rights-based DRR. Ensure humanitarian assistance reaches the most vulnerable, protect against gender-based violence during emergencies, strengthen women's leadership in DRR, and reinforce roles of children, youth, persons with disabilities, and older persons in decision-making on DRR.

principles.title: Safety Net Based Approaches
principles.summary: Establish economic and social safety nets that function equally well during preparedness, emergency response, recovery and reconstruction. Covers disaster finance management schemes (financing, risk financing/insurance, and funds), security mechanisms to protect life and assets, protection mechanisms that compensate victims, and relocation from hazardous areas as a last resort.

principles.title: Multi-Hazard Approaches
principles.summary: Address myriad natural and human-induced/technological hazards through inclusive risk-informed decision-making based on disaggregated data, open exchange of information, and science-based non-sensitive risk information complemented by traditional knowledge. Emphasizes multi-scenario damage anticipation and thorough communication of results to stakeholders.

principles.title: Cross-Cutting Approaches
principles.summary: Integrate DRR across multiple sectors (local government, agriculture, lands, environment, infrastructure, water, education, health, national security, economy, foreign affairs, iTaukei affairs, women, communication) through multi-stakeholder consultation, public-private partnerships, business continuity planning, mass media involvement, and resilience of national health systems.

principles.title: Coordination Mechanisms
principles.summary: Address coordination gaps between policies and institutional arrangements at national, local and community levels, and between structural and non-structural DRR measures. Calls for a focal point agency to coordinate DRR tasks and programmes, and formation of network mechanisms among stakeholders to consolidate knowledge and establish partnerships.

principles.title: Approaches to Disaster Risk Reduction
principles.summary: Focus on tackling underlying disaster risk factors such as poverty, unplanned urbanisation, poor land management, climate change, weak institutional arrangements, and non-risk-informed policies. Emphasizes integration of climate change adaptation and DRR, good governance, people-centred preventive approaches, and full engagement of all institutions of executive and legislative officers.

focusAreas.title: Building Macroeconomic Confidence and Stability
focusAreas.summary: Fiji is forecast to experience growth of 2.8% in 2024 and 3% in 2025-2026. The focus is on strengthening macroeconomic stability by narrowing the trade deficit, achieving price stability through prudent monetary and fiscal policy, improving the fiscal position through judicious expenditure consistent with revenue and debt strategy, and maintaining low and stable inflation with adequate foreign reserves.

focusAreas.title: Fostering International and Regional Relations
focusAreas.summary: Fiji's foreign policy is underpinned by three pillars — sovereignty (safeguarding territorial integrity, promoting Fiji as a regional hub), security (promoting democracy, rule of law, human rights, strengthening security alliances), and prosperity (poverty alleviation, improving economic position of indigenous Fijians, trade expansion, FDI).

focusAreas.title: Sustainably Managing Natural Resources
focusAreas.summary: Focuses on enhancing sugar through cogeneration, climate-resilient varieties and value addition; strengthening non-sugar crops and livestock for food security and commercial agriculture; sustainable forest management with private sector participation; improving land access through institutional and legislative reforms; sustainable development of mineral and groundwater resources; and sustainable management of offshore and inshore fisheries and aquaculture.

focusAreas.title: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
focusAreas.summary: Promotes greater private sector participation as the driver of economic growth by reducing regulatory impediments, reducing bureaucratic red tape, addressing labour and talent constraints, improving land access, giving special attention to MSMEs to increase their contribution to GDP, and rationalising the role of Government through SOE divestment where appropriate.

focusAreas.title: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
focusAreas.summary: Takes a holistic approach to uplifting social wellbeing including addressing poverty (target 18% by 2030), education, healthcare, affordable housing, urban development, empowering women, and the protection of children and people with disabilities. Government continues free primary, secondary and tertiary education, enhances TVET, expands primary and secondary healthcare, and addresses NCDs.

focusAreas.title: Developing Public Infrastructure, Protecting Environment and Addressing Climate Change
focusAreas.summary: Aims to systematically improve the accessibility, quality and efficiency of infrastructure to support growth and enhance the standard of living. Focuses on achieving an integrated, eco-friendly and safe transport system; transforming the energy sector to be resilient and renewable-based; increasing access to clean water and sanitation; improving solid waste management; and strengthening resilience to climate change and natural disasters.

focusAreas.title: Committing to Governance, Institutional and State-Owned Entity Reforms
focusAreas.summary: Emphasises strengthening governance and undertaking institutional reforms to support holistic, effective and efficient implementation of the Plan. Encompasses civil service reforms, Rule of Law and Justice, State Administration and Parliament, and State-Owned Entities. Core commitments include reviewing the 2013 Constitution, ensuring separation and independence of the three arms of Government, and having zero tolerance for corruption.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Sustainably Managing Natural Resources
subChapters.title: Sugar
subChapters.summary: Aims to revitalise the declining sugar industry (contribution fell from 3% to 1% of GDP) through milling efficiency improvements, cogeneration, ethanol plants, climate-resilient cane varieties, quality standards, intercropping, value-added products, youth attraction, and review of institutions and legislations.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Sustainably Managing Natural Resources
subChapters.title: Non-Sugar, Crops and Livestock
subChapters.summary: Seeks a competitive, resilient and sustainable agriculture sector contributing 7% of GDP and employing ~98,000 farmers. Focus areas include food and nutrition security, crop diversification, commercial agriculture for major commodities, improved market access, climate-smart agriculture, youth and women participation, and iTaukei business venture ownership.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Sustainably Managing Natural Resources
subChapters.title: Forestry
subChapters.summary: Aims for sustainable management of Fiji's 1.1 million hectares of forest (60% of land area). Strategies include strengthening sustainable forest management, reviewing policies and laws (Forest Act 1992, REDD+ Policy), encouraging private sector plantation investment, promoting wood and non-wood forest products, carbon trading (first SIDS with ERPA), and the 30 million trees in 15 years campaign.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Sustainably Managing Natural Resources
subChapters.title: Land Management and Development
subChapters.summary: Aims to mobilise iTaukei and state land for economic empowerment. Almost 90% of land is under customary ownership. Strategies include reviewing the State Lands Act and Land Use Act, formulating a Valuation Act and Groundwater Management Act, establishing a Land Use Master Plan, digitalising lease applications, fast-tracking approvals, initiating iTaukei land legislation reforms, and promoting solesolevaki framework for equity ownership.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Sustainably Managing Natural Resources
subChapters.title: Mineral and Groundwater Resources
subChapters.summary: Focuses on sustainable development of groundwater and mineral resources (mining contributes 0.5% of GDP). Strategies include reviewing the Mining Act 1965, Quarries Act 1939 and Explosives Act 1937, developing groundwater extraction guidelines, updating the groundwater inventory, empowering communities in water management, and building capacity in geosciences.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Sustainably Managing Natural Resources
subChapters.title: Marine Resources
subChapters.summary: Aims for sustainable management, development and protection of Fiji's fisheries across offshore, inshore and aquaculture sectors within the ~1.28 million sq km EEZ. Strategies include comprehensive review of fisheries laws, finalising the National Fisheries Policy, strengthening regional trade agreements, implementing electronic monitoring to combat IUU fishing, enhancing aquaculture PPP framework, and promoting women and youth participation.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Trade and Market Access
subChapters.summary: Aims to enhance Fiji's trade and economic position globally through a revamped Trade Policy Framework 2025-2030, participation in IPEF, WTO commitments, export diversification, simplification of cross-border trade, enhancement of digital trade and e-commerce, improvement of national quality infrastructure, and strengthening supply chain resilience.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Private Sector Growth and Participation
subChapters.summary: Seeks to promote private sector participation by creating a conducive ecosystem — reviewing the Investment Act 2021, streamlining regulatory processes including digitalisation of business permits (FILPAS), building human capital, improving access to finance for MSMEs, strengthening institutions and judiciary, and attracting FDI. Target: Investment to GDP of 20%.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Manufacturing
subChapters.summary: Aims to position Fiji as an e-commerce and innovation hub with sustainable manufacturing and export diversification. The sector contributes ~19.8% of GDP and employs 13.9% of paid workforce. Strategies include improving quality of domestic production, expanding industrial base, increasing value addition, and expanding private investment.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Tourism
subChapters.summary: Aims for a greener and innovative tourism industry, contributing ~40% of GDP and as the largest formal employer. Strategies include developing a Tourism Act, introducing sustainable tourism standards, targeting niche segments (luxury, MICE, medical, sports, eco-tourism), creating linkages with agriculture and fisheries, and strengthening community-based tourism.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Creative Industries
subChapters.summary: Seeks to enhance MSME contribution from 18% to 22% of GDP and from 60% to 65% of employment. Strategies include improving access to finance through FDB, digitisation, establishing a Central Online Database for MSMEs, strengthening MSME infrastructure in municipalities, re-introducing credit guarantee schemes, and developing micro-insurance products.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Audio Visual Industry
subChapters.summary: Aims to strengthen and promote the AV industry which generated $444.21 million in 2019. Strategies include implementing recommendations from the ADB Economic Study, reviewing Film Fiji Act 2002, creating an audio-visual ecosystem, promoting Fiji as a filming destination, and building capacity of local crew and filmmakers.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Financial Services
subChapters.summary: Aims for a sustainable financial services sector contributing 20.7% of GDP. Strategies include reviewing and modernising the Banking Act 1995, Insurance Act 1998 and Credit Union Act 1954, strengthening financial literacy, promoting insurance uptake, increasing digitalisation of payments, improving protection against financial fraud, promoting financial inclusion, and developing capital markets for MSMEs.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Construction Industry
subChapters.summary: Aims for a robust, sustainable and resilient construction sector contributing 2.9% to GDP. Strategies include reviewing the National Building Code, introducing builder licensing legislation, addressing the skills shortage exacerbated by emigration, enhancing climate resilience and green building practices, and promoting entrepreneurship.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Outsourcing Industry
subChapters.summary: Aims to leverage Fiji as a leading outsourcing hub generating $200 million revenue and employing 8,000 workers (target 25,000 by 2030). Strategies include strengthening the Investment Act and Immigration Act for outsourcing, establishing Special Economic Zones, developing focused incentives for MNEs, market diversification, and designing digital skills training.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Information and Communications Technology
subChapters.summary: Aims for a resource-efficient, cost-effective ICT sector fostering the digital economy. Strategies include adopting a National Digital Strategy, strengthening cybersecurity (National Cybersecurity Strategy), facilitating 5G deployment, improving digital inclusion and literacy, expanding online government services, and strengthening data sharing across government.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Catalysing Economic Growth and Diversifying the Economy
subChapters.title: Research and Development and Innovation
subChapters.summary: Aims to promote RDI and adopt advanced technologies including IR 4.0 and AI to accelerate economic growth. Currently minimal RDI investment. Strategies include formulating a National Policy on Science, Technology and Innovation, establishing a Triple Helix Model (academia-government-industry), creating centres of excellence and a Science and Technology park, and expanding RDI funding options.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Poverty Alleviation and Social Protection
subChapters.summary: 24.1% of Fijians (~258,000 individuals) live under the Basic Needs Poverty Line. Strategies include developing income-generating opportunities under the Integrated National Poverty Eradication Programme, expanding social protection (Family Assistance Scheme, Social Pension Scheme supporting ~26,200 elderly, Bus Fare Concession), poverty graduation programmes, and conditional cash transfers.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Healthcare
subChapters.summary: Aims to modernise Fiji's healthcare system. NCDs account for over 70% of premature deaths. Strategies include establishing programmes to control NCDs, strengthening mental health services, providing comprehensive life-cycle healthcare, improving healthcare literacy, fostering R&D in healthcare, expanding primary healthcare, modernising health infrastructure, and addressing the exodus of medical professionals.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Education and Training
subChapters.summary: Aims to nurture innovative lifelong learners through quality education delivery. Net enrolment: ~100% primary, ~80% secondary. Strategies include reviewing the Education Act 1966 and other key legislations, improving LANA achievement rates, strengthening TVET and MATUA programmes, improving teacher-to-student ratios (target 1:40 primary, 1:30 secondary), expanding ECCE, and establishing the Fiji National Research Council.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Housing
subChapters.summary: Aims to provide accessible and adequate housing. Approximately 25% of urban population live in over 250 informal settlements. Strategies include the IFC PPP Project to supply ~3,000 affordable housing units, upgrading informal settlements (target 6 formalised/upgraded), providing first-time homeowner grants, promoting green building practices, strengthening the rental market, and developing resilient rural housing.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Urban Development
subChapters.summary: Aims for resilient and environmentally sustainable urban centres. Approximately 58% of population resides in urban areas. Strategies include reviewing legislative and policy frameworks, enhancing service delivery, undertaking climate change modelling and hazard mapping for all urban centres, strengthening urban management at municipal level, and developing spatial plans with 20-year miniature models.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Rural and Outer Island Development
subChapters.summary: 94% of Fiji's land area constitutes rural and outer islands with 44.7% of population residing there. Strategies include expanding access to rural infrastructure (roads, jetties, bridges, seawalls, electrification, water supply), improving connectivity and accessibility, promoting sustainable rural economic activities, strengthening the Integrated Rural Development Framework, and mainstreaming disaster risk reduction in all aspects of rural development.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Population, Employment and Labour Market
subChapters.summary: Population estimated at 900,886 in 2025 with 69% below age 40. Unemployment rate at 4.3% (lowest in 20 years) with target 3.8%. Strategies include reviewing and modernising employment relations framework, strengthening workplace compliance, improving labour market services, strengthening participation in Labour Mobility Programmes (PALM Scheme, RSE), addressing skill gaps, and implementing the National Productivity Master Plan.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Protection of Children, Youth and People with Disabilities
subChapters.summary: Aims to provide a safe and conducive environment. Child abuse cases increased from 838 (2018) to 1,968 (2022). Over 50% of population is under 34. Strategies include aligning child protection legislation to UNCRC, strengthening safety and care (Child Protection Allowances), preventing child abuse including finalising the Volatile Substance Abuse Bill, promoting youth education and training for decent employment, empowering youth participation, and ensuring rights and accessibility for persons with disabilities.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Culture and Heritage
subChapters.summary: Aims to promote and protect Fiji's diverse cultural heritage. Strategies include reviewing the iTaukei Affairs Act 1944, Fiji Museum Act 1929 and National Trust of Fiji Act 1970, implementing the National Cultural Policy, completing cultural mapping of all 14 provinces, establishing a Cultural Tourism Framework, digitalising the Vola ni Kawa Bula, and integrating culture into the formal education curriculum.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Sports Development
subChapters.summary: Aims to develop talent and achieve sporting excellence. Sports tourism contributed $67.1 million and created 21,000 employment opportunities in 2023. Strategies include establishing a National Sports Talent Identification System, promoting sports as a mechanism for economic development, developing sports facilities and sports medicine infrastructure, hosting major international events, and increasing female sports participation.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: iTaukei Participation in Development
subChapters.summary: Aims to strengthen iTaukei involvement through inclusive development. Key initiatives include institutional review of iTaukei institutions (TAB, TLFC, TLTB, TTFB, CATD, FHL), joint approach through the Solesolevaki framework (4-phase structure from landowner investment to market access), natural resource development, indigenous participation in business, unlocking the culture and heritage sector, and improving socioeconomic wellbeing of iTaukei people.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Uplifting Socioeconomic Wellbeing
subChapters.title: Women in Economic Development
subChapters.summary: Aims to empower women to increase economic contribution. Women's composition in paid employment increased from 36.8% (2018) to 37.2% (2019). Only 19% of registered MSMEs list women as owners. Strategies include improving access to income-generating activities, promoting women in leadership and STEM, reducing violence through coordinated referral networks, strengthening the Gender Budget Template, and encouraging greater women participation in formal and informal sector employment.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Developing Public Infrastructure, Protecting Environment and Addressing Climate Change
subChapters.title: Transport
subChapters.summary: Seeks an integrated, eco-friendly, safe, accessible and efficient transportation system. Land transport assets valued at ~$11 billion with over $1.7 billion allocated over 5 years. Strategies include upgrading and maintaining roads, ports, wharves, rural airstrips; improving public transport; promoting electric vehicles; decarbonising maritime transport; expanding air connectivity through bilateral open skies agreements; and establishing a Transport Master Plan. Target: reduce road fatalities from 72 to 36.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Developing Public Infrastructure, Protecting Environment and Addressing Climate Change
subChapters.title: Energy and Electricity
subChapters.summary: Seeks a resilient, resource-efficient, energy sector with ~98% electricity access. EFL produced 55.3% from renewables in 2022 with a mission for 90% renewable by 2025. Strategies include improving access to affordable renewable energy, increasing private sector participation by reviewing the Electricity Act 2017, upgrading infrastructure, enhancing energy efficiency, and strengthening resilience of energy infrastructure to climate impacts. Target: 100% renewable energy share in electricity generation.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Developing Public Infrastructure, Protecting Environment and Addressing Climate Change
subChapters.title: Water and Wastewater
subChapters.summary: Seeks sustainable management of water and sanitation. 82% of population have access to treated water but only 28% to central sewerage. Non-revenue water stands at 48%. Strategies include finalising the National Water Resource Management and Sanitation Policy, corporatising WAF, formulating the Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Master Plan, expanding access, promoting desalination and ecological purification systems, and ensuring long-term freshwater resource security. Target: 88% total population access to clean water.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Developing Public Infrastructure, Protecting Environment and Addressing Climate Change
subChapters.title: Solid Waste Management
subChapters.summary: Seeks a sustainable waste management system. Only 0.2% of waste was recycled in 2021. Strategies include establishing a landfill and recycling plant in the Western Division, introducing recycling programmes, enhancing compliance with single-use plastic bag bans, promoting circular economy approaches, upgrading healthcare waste infrastructure, and reviewing waste management legislation.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Developing Public Infrastructure, Protecting Environment and Addressing Climate Change
subChapters.title: Environment and Climate Change
subChapters.summary: Seeks sustainable and integrated approaches against climate change. Fiji recorded 0.9°C temperature rise since 1959 and 3-4mm/year sea-level rise. Energy sector accounts for 52.7% of GHG emissions. Strategies include institutionalising climate risk management, accelerating resilient development through national compliance standards, improving national capacity for strategic foresight, integrating climate projections across all sector plans, preserving natural carbon sinks, operationalising the Warsaw International Mechanism for Loss and Damage, and leveraging international climate finance.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Developing Public Infrastructure, Protecting Environment and Addressing Climate Change
subChapters.title: National Disaster Risk Reduction
subChapters.summary: Seeks building resilience through risk-informed development. TC Winston (2016) caused $2 billion in economic impact affecting 540,000 people. Fiji needs an estimated $9.3 billion over 10 years for climate resilience investment. Strategies include strengthening integration of climate and disaster risk in development planning, developing a Disaster Risk Financing Policy, strengthening multi-hazard early warning systems, establishing resilient multipurpose evacuation centres, and mainstreaming DRR at the local level.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Committing to Governance, Institutional and State-Owned Entity Reforms
subChapters.title: Rule of Law and Justice
subChapters.summary: Aims to ensure safety, security and wellbeing of Fiji and all Fijians. Strategies include reviewing the 2013 Constitution, strengthening regulatory and legal framework, ensuring independent judiciary, upgrading court facilities, expanding legal aid services (LAC offices grew from 18 to 27), strengthening police professionalism (review of Police Act 1965), establishing a Drugs and Narcotics Bureau, combating corruption (target PCI score of 60 from baseline 52), and upholding human rights.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Committing to Governance, Institutional and State-Owned Entity Reforms
subChapters.title: State Administration and Parliament
subChapters.summary: Aims to strengthen democracy through effective Parliament and State Institutions. Parliament has 55 seats with 6 Standing Committees. Strategies include strengthening Parliamentary processes and ICT infrastructure, supporting MPs with capacity building, re-establishing the independent Parliamentary Counsel, strengthening core public sector agencies (reviewing Audit Act 1969 and Statistics Act 1961), improving fiscal transparency, and conducting free and fair elections.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Committing to Governance, Institutional and State-Owned Entity Reforms
subChapters.title: Civil Service Reforms
subChapters.summary: Aims to develop a modern, high-performing Civil Service responsive to Government priorities. Civil service employs over 30,000 (~32,092 as of April 2024) with salary/wage spending at 8.7% of GDP. Approximately 15% of positions remain vacant due to outward migration. Strategies include right-sizing the public service to ~25,000, reviewing remuneration and salary structure, developing an effective Performance Management System, establishing the Fiji Learning Institute for Public Service, strengthening transparency and accountability, and decentralising public services.

subChapters.focusAreaTitle: Committing to Governance, Institutional and State-Owned Entity Reforms
subChapters.title: State-Owned Entities
subChapters.summary: Aims for high-performing SOEs with enhanced accountability, transparency and governance. 19 active SOEs contribute 3.7% to GDP but control 16-20% of gross fixed investment. Average Return on Equity at 4% and Return on Asset at 2.1%. Strategies include enhancing SOE performance through commercialisation, expanding private sector involvement (divestment/sale), formulating a privatisation policy framework, improving accountability through publishing annual reports, developing merit-based board director selection guidelines, and divesting shares in EFL, PAFCO and AFL to iTaukei investors.

xFactors.title: Promoting Private Sector Participation in the Economy and Rationalising the Role of Government
xFactors.rationale: Fiji's real GDP growth has averaged 2-3% over the last decade, below its potential. Private sector participation is limited to few sectors, constrained by heavy regulatory burden and high cost of doing business. Government involvement through SOEs crowds out private investment. Opening space for private investment can unleash higher growth trajectory.
xFactors.whatWillBeDone: Government will create a conducive ecosystem by reducing policy and regulatory impediments, reducing bureaucratic red tape, addressing labour and talent constraints, improving land access, and considering appropriate incentives. MSMEs will receive special attention to increase their GDP contribution. Government will open new opportunities for private investment in areas like public infrastructure, housing, healthcare and tertiary education through PPPs. Government will rationalise its participation in the economy through SOEs by gradually divesting where appropriate.

xFactors.title: Promoting Research and Development and Innovation and Technology Adoption
xFactors.rationale: Currently minimal RDI activities in both public and private sectors with a general lack of understanding of its importance. Given the onset of the 4th Industrial Revolution driven by digitalisation, Fiji needs to adopt and apply these technologies across all aspects of operation and development to increase productivity, raise incomes, create new high-value jobs, move up the value chain and diversify the economic base.
xFactors.whatWillBeDone: Government in consultation with the private sector will create and implement the policy, strategy and institutional framework for RDI and promote technology adoption. RDI initiatives will focus on strategic areas consistent with development priorities (agriculture, manufacturing, services, environmental conservation, disaster risk management). Special attention will be on Artificial Intelligence. Government will consider appropriate incentives, funding modalities including a match grant scheme, and capacity building to support RDI.

xFactors.title: Intensifying Rural and Outer Island Transformation
xFactors.rationale: Development in rural and outer islands has lagged and the rural-urban gap has widened, although slightly less than half the population resides in these areas. Poverty incidence is higher in rural areas. Access to basic facilities like clean water, electricity, proper sanitation, internet connectivity is lacking. Poor condition of rural roads, bridges and jetties limits mobility. Schools and healthcare facilities need upgrading. These areas are more vulnerable to natural disasters and climate change, which has also driven rural-to-urban migration.
xFactors.whatWillBeDone: The NDP will intensify efforts and allocate greater resources for rural and outer island development to ensure balanced development. Measures include improving connectivity through better roads and jetties, providing basic infrastructure (bridges, seawalls, electricity, water, drainage, transportation, communication), prioritising rural road construction and maintenance, promoting sustainable and resilient resource-based economic activities, improving schools and healthcare access, and mainstreaming disaster risk reduction.

xFactors.title: Strengthening Resilience against the Impacts of Natural Disaster and Climate Change
xFactors.rationale: Fiji is highly exposed and vulnerable to natural disasters and climate change due to its geographic location and topography. TC Winston caused significant property loss and set back economic and social progress. Measures to strengthen resilience must be taken in parallel with strategies for economic growth and social wellbeing to safeguard development gains.
xFactors.whatWillBeDone: The NDP introduces a comprehensive policy and strategy framework including mainstreaming climate resilience and disaster risk reduction in development planning (infrastructure, spatial and sector planning), enforcing stricter compliance to related standards and codes, increasing investment in adaptation measures, increasing national capability for risk foresight and early detection, establishing the National Disaster Management Office, developing a joint action plan for climate change and DRR, developing a Disaster Risk Financing Policy with innovative financing solutions, and strengthening the multi-hazard warning system with a people-centred approach.

xFactors.title: Commitment to Implementation and Accountability
xFactors.rationale: A plan defeats its purpose if not implemented and progress not monitored. Good governance requires institutionalised platforms for people to hold Government accountable. An IME framework is essential for timely implementation, optimised resource allocation, improved programme effectiveness, and enabling stakeholder engagement and feedback to take corrective measures.
xFactors.whatWillBeDone: The NDP is underpinned by an integrated IME framework to track quarterly and yearly implementation. Policies and strategies are accompanied by high-level outcomes which will be the KPIs of respective Permanent Secretaries. Ministries will develop credible and realistic outputs and report quarterly and annually. A Cabinet Sub-Committee on IME will be established to safeguard taxpayer funds, optimise resource utilisation and maximise policy impacts. Public reporting will include quarterly publications and an annual report card.

allActions.summary: Support development of REDD+ and ocean initiatives, including sustainable forest and coast management and conservation to ensure long-term benefits to the environment and for natural resource-dependent communities.

allActions.parentTitle: Low Carbon Development
allActions.label: (j)
allActions.summary: Assist relevant PICTs to establish, implement and maintain monitoring systems that use an appropriate combination of remote sensing and ground-based carbon inventory approaches, in support of strengthening sustainable forest management efforts at national and subnational levels.

allActions.parentTitle: Low Carbon Development
allActions.label: (k)
allActions.summary: Work with PICTs to assess and implement ways to enhance and maintain natural carbon reservoirs in both marine and terrestrial ecosystems.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (a)
allActions.summary: Review and strengthen disaster risk management planning arrangements and legislation, ensuring clearly defined roles and responsibilities and an inclusive approach involving all stakeholders including international and multi-stakeholder support to response and recovery.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (b)
allActions.summary: Conduct post-disaster needs assessments, using standardised methodologies updated to the extent possible and baseline data to inform recovery planning.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (c)
allActions.summary: Ensure the acquisition, use and sharing of accurate data and other information, including sex-and-age disaggregated data and data for vulnerable groups, to assess risk and facilitate more focused preparedness, response and recovery activities, as well as for loss and damage assessment.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (d)
allActions.summary: Strengthen capacities at the national government, local government and community level to develop integrated preparedness and response plans through inclusive gender-responsive decision-making systems, human rights-based approaches, and sound financial management to plan for and ensure fast and effective humanitarian action, disaster response and recovery.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (e)
allActions.summary: Include the private sector, especially the logistics, telecommunications and tourism sectors, in national planning for all phases of disaster risk management.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (f)
allActions.summary: Support existing and additional capacity-building and awareness raising for governments and communities (including churches and schools), to improve their disaster preparedness, response and recovery capabilities, acknowledging they are often the first responders in the event of a disaster.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (g)
allActions.summary: Improve country-level humanitarian coordination mechanisms by adequately resourcing the national disaster management office and emergency operations centres and ensuring appropriate coordination with all relevant partners and regional disaster management mechanisms.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (h)
allActions.summary: Strengthen effective multi-hazard early warning systems including for sudden and slow onset hazards and the use of science and technology to inform risk management and hazard/disaster preparedness and policy development.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (i)
allActions.summary: Ensure early warning language and messages are accessible to managers and decision makers, civil society and communities, ensuring that messaging and the availability of humanitarian services reaches vulnerable groups.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (j)
allActions.summary: Ensure communication infrastructure and two-way communication channels are available to affected people in disasters through channels that are used within the country and communities.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (k)
allActions.summary: Anticipate and prepare for future displacement by integrating human mobility issues within disaster preparedness, response and recovery programmes and actions.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (l)
allActions.summary: Support increasing the protection of individuals and communities most vulnerable to climate change and post-disaster displacement and migration through targeted national and regional policies and regional labour migration schemes.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (m)
allActions.summary: Ensure that finance and planning institutions play a central role in strategic, whole-of-country approaches for preparedness, response, and recovery, and that all opportunities for climate change and risk financing including insurance are pursued, with support from regional agencies.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (n)
allActions.summary: Provide an enabling environment for effective partnership with the private sector, civil society and other stakeholders for improved preparedness, response and recovery; develop public-private partnership agreements with businesses and members of the private sector so that systems are ready for times of emergency.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (o)
allActions.summary: Collect post-disaster time series information that separates elements of the cause (hazard, vulnerability and exposure) and the effect (impact or consequence) to inform estimates of future impacts (risk assessments) and to monitor progress toward risk reduction targets.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (p)
allActions.summary: Maintain and update knowledge management systems, and ensure that lessons learned during and in the aftermath of emergencies and disasters are included.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (q)
allActions.summary: Strengthen the inter-operability of systems used by key national response agencies to plan for improved coordination of response efforts and the optimisation of available resources.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (r)
allActions.summary: Establish a contingency stockpile of emergency relief items.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (a)
allActions.summary: Work with partners to strengthen capacity to effectively serve as first responders in emergencies and disasters.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (b)
allActions.summary: Strengthen capacity in all aspects of disaster management, including gender-sensitive disaster preparedness and response arrangements and plans for communities, while addressing the specific needs of vulnerable groups aligned with plans, mechanisms and arrangements of national governments.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (c)
allActions.summary: Encourage a spiritually, theologically and culturally inclusive approach that underpins personal involvement in strengthening disaster preparedness, response and recovery.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (d)
allActions.summary: Encourage protection of human rights in the context of climate change and disasters and to use appropriate methods that ensure inclusive participation of vulnerable groups to address their specific needs.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (a)
allActions.summary: Work with other partners to strengthen disaster management capacity, including leading and participating in joint disaster scenario planning, response, and recovery.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (b)
allActions.summary: Support community preparedness and emergency response, such as using mobile and radio technologies as tools/platforms for raising awareness and education, and for early warning and alerts, to ensure messaging and the availability of humanitarian services reaches communities including vulnerable groups.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (c)
allActions.summary: Build and strengthen private-public sector partnerships to facilitate agreements in place prior to an emergency, and to stimulate knowledge sharing and innovative solutions for improving disaster preparedness, response and recovery.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (d)
allActions.summary: Develop and implement business continuity plans according to best practice, and incorporate risk financing options such as liability and insurance regimes into these plans including for small-scale businesses and producers.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (e)
allActions.summary: Strengthen investments in post-disaster recovery using low carbon development, climate change resilience solutions, build back better and build back safer approaches to reduce future disaster risks and impacts from climate change.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (f)
allActions.summary: Facilitate sector needs and capacity mapping including an inventory of private sector resources and services that can be made available before and after a disaster event in ways that assist response and recovery efforts.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (a)
allActions.summary: Support the strengthening of capacities (including humanitarian coordination mechanisms) and planning arrangements at regional, national and subnational level (including through community-based approaches) to better prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (b)
allActions.summary: Strengthen end-to-end early warning systems through effective processes and interoperability.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (c)
allActions.summary: Ensure optimum use of resources and capacities for emergency/disaster response by supporting PICTs in their efforts to strengthen interoperability of key response agencies and systems.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (d)
allActions.summary: Provide technical advice and support to develop disaster management strategies and plans that are gender-responsive and include human rights-based approaches.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (e)
allActions.summary: Assist in strengthening the telecommunications, observational data and data processing infrastructure that supports provision of reliable early warnings and hazard/risk information.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (f)
allActions.summary: Encourage the public finance management and disaster risk management communities to work together to improve technical assistance training.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (g)
allActions.summary: Support the ongoing development of national and regional financing modalities that will promote improved access to relevant funding mechanisms for disaster response and climate change.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (h)
allActions.summary: Work with other development partners, governments and administrations to support building resilience of the private sector and their contributions to disaster risk management including: facilitating capacity mapping and private sector resource inventory, aligning supply chain practices for cost efficiencies, and timely delivery of emergency supplies and services.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
allActions.label: (i)
allActions.summary: Develop guidelines, including best practice models, for effective disaster risk management at national and subnational level.

allActions.parentTitle: Strengthened Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery
